about_intro_html: I'm Sayantan Sen — a technology executive by day, and as of this project, a first-time developer by night. I'm VP of Technology Services at GlobalLogic (a Hitachi Group company), based in San Jose, California. This website is itself part of that story: I'm building and coding it myself, learning Python and web development along the way, rather than just describing that I lead engineering teams for a living.
professional_journey_html:
My path into technology wasn't planned as a straight line toward leadership — it started, quite literally, at the code level.

I began my career in 2000 as a developer and database architect, writing Java and Oracle PL/SQL for Apple's internal Directory Services platform — the system that tracked employees, contractors, vendors, and hardware across the company, tied into HR systems and LDAP under a 24x7 support model. It was unglamorous, deadline-driven work, and it taught me two things that have stayed with me ever since: production systems don't forgive sloppy thinking, and the people who keep them running rarely get the credit they deserve.

Over the next decade at Infosys, I moved steadily from writing code to designing systems to leading the teams that built them — solution architecture and delivery for clients like Molex, Solectron, Boeing, Cisco, and Microsoft, much of it in the unglamorous but essential world of B2B and EDI integration: gateways, mapping migrations, supplier onboarding — the plumbing that lets large companies actually talk to each other. A short stint at Software AG building out a North American delivery practice sharpened a different muscle: not just delivering programs, but building the organization that delivers them.

The next chapter, at IBM, is where the scope really opened up. I ran multi-year, multi-country programs for Lowe's, Tesco, Forever 21, T-Mobile, and Abbott — order management modernization, supply chain integration, platform launches across dozens of workstreams and international teams. Then came Caterpillar: a five-year engagement where I owned the technical and commercial evolution of their B2B/B2C digital commerce platform, including a first-of-its-kind mobile payment integration (WeChat Pay, Alipay, UnionPay) for their dealer network, and the security architecture behind it — cryptographic request signing, merchant key custody, the unglamorous but critical work of making sure a payment system can't be spoofed. That platform grew from roughly half a million dollars to over $120M in annual revenue under my watch, across seven countries and 70+ integrated systems.

Since 2020, I've been Vice President and Chief of Staff to the Chief Delivery Officer at GlobalLogic, where the job has shifted again — from running individual programs to shaping how a 20,000+ person global engineering organization operates. Today that means leading enterprise AI strategy: defining how GenAI and agentic AI get evaluated, adopted, and governed across a company this size, running technical and commercial evaluations of frontier model providers, and personally building the prototypes and automation that inform those decisions. It also means owning a $300M+ portfolio of strategic client programs and the operating rhythm — planning, forecasting, executive reviews — that keeps a global organization moving in the same direction.

Looking back, the throughline isn't really "developer to executive." It's that I've never stopped wanting to understand how things actually work underneath — which is, not coincidentally, exactly why I'm building this website myself instead of hiring someone to do it.
